children: Canada and the European Union will begin talks next month on a new security and economic alliance, the latest bold step by Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney to reduce his country's economic reliance on the U.S.

Carney delivered the news Tuesday at an investment summit he's hosting in Toronto, where some of the world's biggest investors--from Wall Street heavyweights to sovereign-wealth funds--are attending as the Canadian leader makes a pitch for their investment dollars.
Late Tuesday, Carney is traveling to Europe where he's set to deliver remarks to the European Parliament. In remarks, Carney provided a preview of what's ahead.
"Next month, we will begin discussions with the EU - the world's second-largest economy - to build a unique security and economic alliance," Carney said.

The Wall Street Journal reported on Saturday that Carney instructed his special envoy to Europe to scope out the most ambitious possibilities short of full membership in the EU or its common market, according to people familiar with the matter. Canadian and European officials are discussing ways for Canada to informally lock into Europe's $20 trillion single market in key supply chains, the Journal reported.

The move to seek a special alliance with the EU comes amid a sharp deterioration in trade ties between Ottawa and Washington. The two capitals are mired in a heightened trade conflict after talks on a tariff collapsed last month. Both countries have now imposed hefty tariffs on each other's exports.
Carney said that Canada would continue to be the U.S.'s most important partner in many key areas.

"These arrangements work when we engage as true partners that respect each other's traditions and sovereignty," he said. "When those opportunities return, Canada will be an even better partner-stronger, more resilient, more independent-ready to advance our mutual economic and security interests."

title: Canada, EU to Begin Talks on 'Unique' Alliance Next Month, Carney Says
